candidates.title: Crash that killed 4 teens in Puslinch, Ont., an 'unimaginable tragedy': police
candidates.description: Four teens, aged 15 to 19 years, died in a crash in Puslinch, a rural area southeast of Guelph, early Saturday, according to Ontario Provincial Police.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Proposed data centre would release ‘23 Hiroshima-sized atomic bombs worth of energy’ a day, physicist says
candidates.description: An analysis of the mammoth Wonder Valley data centre suggests it would release the equivalent of 23 atom bombs of heat waste into the boreal forest of northwestern Alberta every day. A Utah State University physicist who conducted the review for the Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation said the project demands a full environmental impact assessment.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Medical oncologist based in Brandon, Man., says he's leaving his 'dream job' over lack of support
candidates.description: A medical oncologist based in Brandon is leaving the role in November, saying his repeated calls for support have been ignored by the province.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: In wake of Wainwright tragedy, this year's Silver Cross Mother has a message for grieving families
candidates.description: Virginia Hicks is this year's national Silver Cross Mother, an annual tradition by the Royal Canadian Legion recognizing the mother of a fallen Canadian Armed Forces member each Remembrance Day. Every year she visits CFB Petawawa in the Ottawa Valley, where her daughter Sapper Mariebeth Short was killed during a training exercise in 2002.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: N.S. lobster fishers face mounting pressure from soaring fuel prices
candidates.description: As the season opening looms for southwestern Nova Scotia's lobster zone, fishermen face mounting uncertainty from skyrocketing fuel prices among other concerns.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Don't like daylight saving time? Nova Scotia once lost 11 days in a single night
candidates.description: People in the entire British Empire went to bed on Sept. 2, 1752, and woke up on Sept. 14, 1752.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta woman accused of sex with 15-year-old guilty of sexual assault
candidates.description: Jurors have reached a verdict in Alexa Suitor's sexual assault trial, finding Suitor guilty of sexual assault and sexual interference.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hamilton burn centre sends 9 specialists to help care for soldiers injured in Wainwright fire
candidates.description: Nine burn-care specialists from Hamilton Health Sciences have travelled to Edmonton to help treat military personnel severely injured in the deadly fire at a Canadian Forces base in Wainwright, Alta.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After estimated $360 million in flood damage, why is province saying Niagara residents don't qualify for aid?
candidates.description: The devastating summer floods that hit north Niagara helped propel Canada's total insured damage from natural disasters over the summer to one of the worst on record, new data shows.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Want to catch a Quebec-made film for just $3? Check out these theatres on select Sundays
candidates.description: Starting on Nov. 8, filmgoers will be able to watch Quebec-made movies for just $3 in over a dozen independent cinemas on the second Sunday of each month, for the next year. The goal behind the initiative is to bring more eyes and support to Quebec on the big screen.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mr. PG stuffie hikes to Mount Everest base camp with this B.C. adventurer
candidates.description: Prince George resident Lydia Troc is an adventurer — her latest trip took her up to Mount Everest base camp in Nepal. But she didn't go alone — she took a plushie version of Prince George's beloved mascot Mr. PG.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Rourke leads Lions past Roughriders in CFL West semifinal
candidates.description: Nathan Rourke passed for 366 yards and the B.C. Lions came all the way back to beat the Saskatchewan Roughriders 33-26 in the CFL’s West Division semifinal on Saturday in Vancouver.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Parks Canada set to slash warden detachments, officers across national parks
candidates.description: Detachments will be closing in British Columbia, Alberta, Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Yukon and Northwest Territories. The number of wardens impacted by the decision is unknown, but CBC News has learned at least a dozen positions will be cut.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Drug runner? Arms dealer? The Adeline-C made waves in Halifax and beyond
candidates.description: The Adeline-C arrived in Halifax on Oct. 31, 1981, filled with state-of-the-art equipment, but it was soon abandoned by its crew. It would be years before its role in a complex U.S. drug smuggling operation worth as much as $200 million US became fully known.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's Lia Pereira, Trennt Michaud win pairs gold at Skate Canada International
candidates.description: Canadian figure skaters Lia Pereira and Trennt Michaud won pairs gold at Skate Canada International in Kelowna, B.C., on Saturday, capturing their first Grand Prix title in three years.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cocaine smuggler could avoid prison as judge fears incarceration would orphan 7-year-old son
candidates.description: A Toronto judge is weighing whether to send a single father to prison for importing cocaine into Newfoundland and Labrador during the pandemic, or find an alternate sentence that could "break the cycle" for his seven-year-old boy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Many P.E.I. municipalities are seeing uncontested elections this year. Why aren't more people running?
candidates.description: There are 400 positions up for grabs across 56 municipalities, but many of those positions have already been acclaimed. In a total of 27 municipalities, all positions have been acclaimed, according to P.E.I.'s unofficial election results.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 4 dead, 2 in life-threatening condition after car crash in Puslinch, Ont.
candidates.description: Four people are dead and two others suffered life-threatening injuries after a single-vehicle crash in Puslinch — a rural area southwest of Guelph — early Saturday, according to Ontario Provincial Police.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian Crime Stoppers Association advises chapters to accept tips by phone only
candidates.description: The Canadian Crime Stoppers Association is advising its local chapters to solely accept tips by telephone instead of online, it said in a statement to CBC News on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Prince Harry says he wants to reconcile with the Royal Family. It may not be so easy
candidates.description: As much as Prince Harry may signal his desire to reconcile with the Royal Family, making it happen could be a challenge.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Young men and right-leaning podcasters helped Trump win in 2024. Both have soured on him
candidates.description: Young men are increasingly turned off by U.S. President Donald Trump, and right-leaning podcasters are distancing themselves, too — a trend that experts say could swing House and potential Senate seats in next week's midterms.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's party primary challenger endorses his Republican rival
candidates.description: Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's former opponent in the U.S. Senate primary, Haley Stevens, stunned party officials Sunday by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers after Democratic tensions boiled over days before the election that could determine the balance of power on Capitol Hill.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: German ministers pledge tough action after rioters damage stores in Frankfurt
candidates.description: German ministers threatened tough penalties for looters and rioters who damaged stores and injured more than 100 police officers in Frankfurt overnight, while still praising public forces for preventing larger-scale violence.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge throws out Trump suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
candidates.description: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a U.S. federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10-billion lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to wealthy financier Jeffrey Epstein.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Binance says billions replaced from hack that FBI blames on North Korea
candidates.description: Crypto exchange Binance said on Saturday it has been able to replace 90 per cent of the amount stolen after a record $6.3-billion US hack of its platform. The FBI on Saturday ‌said the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mexico comes alive during annual Day of the Dead celebrations
candidates.description: Festivities begin in October and lead up to Nov. 1 and 2, when the souls of deceased loved ones are believed to temporarily return to earth to reunite with their families.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Democrats and Republicans are joining forces to fight data centres in Ohio
candidates.description: In a time of extreme political polarization in the United States, opposition to AI data centre development is cutting through traditional divides. The bipartisan backlash is especially strong in Ohio, where Republicans and Democrats are putting aside political differences to fight what they see as a common enemy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Civilians evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrive in Ukraine-held territory
candidates.description: Residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have crossed into Ukrainian-held territory after a humanitarian mission and localized ceasefire, part of a major rescue operation carried out under the most significant truce since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Youth-led protests sweep across France, Europe for a 3rd weekend
candidates.description: Hundreds of thousands of mostly young protesters took to the streets across France on Saturday in a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over living costs and education. Youth-led demonstrations were also reported in Germany and Italy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: NASA telescope predicted to plunge back to Earth after failed rescue mission
candidates.description: An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: This Texas midterm race has huge stakes, both for Donald Trump and the country
candidates.description: There's no U.S. midterm election with more at stake than the battle between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico to become the next senator for Texas. The outcome could determine which party holds a majority in the U.S. Senate for the remainder of Donald Trump’s presidency.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'No one is safe' as Ebola outbreak surges to more than 10,000 cases, Africa's top doctor warns Canada
candidates.description: Africa's top doctor, who has called Canada home since 2013, tells CBC News there could be "massive" cross-border spread of Ebola in the months ahead as he calls for more international support.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Decision clearing path for Russia to join world juniors in Alberta is 'very unwelcome,' minister says
candidates.description: Canada's foreign affairs minister says the decision to let Russia back into the ice hockey world championships came as a "great disappointment" on Friday, as the country's ongoing invasion of Ukraine stretches toward its fifth year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Did human error cause Spain's deadly high-speed train crash? | About That
candidates.description: A high-speed train travelling at more than 150 km/h collided with a stopped train in central Spain, killing at least 69 people and injuring dozens more. Andrew Chang breaks down dispatcher audio and information about the railway's signalling system to explain how a technical glitch may have led to the fatal crash. (Photo credits: The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images)
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. charges 5 more Canadians with voter fraud offences amid Trump administration crackdown
candidates.description: The U.S. Department of Justice says charges have been laid against five more Canadians for voting fraud-related offences, the latest in a flurry of similar prosecutions ahead of next week's midterm elections.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
candidates.description: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
candidates.description: The protests in cities across Germany - including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt - came on the same day hundreds of thousands also protested in France.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
candidates.description: The new police unit is a security measure in response to last year's deadly shooting attack at a Hanukkah festival.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat escalates
candidates.description: Haley Stevens, who lost out on the Democratic Senate nomination to Abdul El-Sayed, endorses his opponent days before the vote.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Judge dismisses Trump's lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein birthday book
candidates.description: Trump had sued the media outlet after it published a letter to Epstein purportedly written and signed by the president as part of a birthday book.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
candidates.description: The order comes after election officials received letters demanding they set aside the ballots of possible non-citizen voters.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Alaska Senate candidate denies knowing about alleged plot to put two Dan Sullivans on ballot
candidates.description: The incumbent Republican running for re-election and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters by recruiting a second Dan Sullivan to also stand in the race.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
candidates.description: Oleshky residents had been without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Police deployed during stand-off over control of top Poland court
candidates.description: The escalation came after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
candidates.description: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confronted his Russian counterpart at the meeting and accused his government of killing innocent civilians in Ukraine.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Peaceful protests in Germany spiral into violence and looting
candidates.description: Thousands joined largely orderly demonstrations earlier in the day, before violence erupted in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
candidates.description: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against the rising cost of living and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
candidates.description: The BBC's Dan Johnson travelled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: CCTV and zip ties: How US mail-in votes are secured and counted
candidates.description: BBC Verify goes to an election centre to get a behind-the-scenes look at how mail-in ballots for the US midterm elections are processed.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Lindsay Clancy is back in court - where will her case go next?
candidates.description: The Massachusetts mother, accused of murdering her three children, is expected back in court as she awaits a decision on whether her case will be retried.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?
candidates.description: The state's $500m Senate race may be the most closely watched in the US midterms, and is about far more than control of Congress.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
candidates.description: Defeat for Serbia's Aleksandar Vučiċ in last weekend's vote was a carbon copy of Viktor Orbán's fall in Hungary.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: I've been stuck on a tiny Pacific island for years and can't get a transit visa to fly home
candidates.description: Ruchira Ranasingha, 50, has been stranded in the Cook Islands since 2023 and wants to return to Sri Lanka.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The fight to save Canadian town threatened by Trump's tariffs
candidates.description: A century-old paper mill in Témiscaming, Quebec is indefinitely closed after the US imposed 50% tariffs on its products, putting hundreds out of work.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
candidates.description: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Oil tank vandalism results in waterfowl park 'nightmare'
candidates.description: The popular attraction in County Down has been forced to close while efforts continue to remove oil from the pond.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Rok' solid recognition for Slovenian space scientist
candidates.description: Two men from the Armagh Planetarium and Observatory have had asteroids named in their honour in recognition of their work.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: UK could see 10 days without rain after 'wettest week in two years'
candidates.description: With high pressure developing across the UK, the start of November is looking very settled with no significant rain in the forecast.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Aquarium shark that helped 'dispel myths' dies
candidates.description: Staff at Plymouth's aquarium pay tribute to a sand tiger shark believed to be almost 30 years old.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: They signed up for a lifetime at sea on an endless cruise. High gas prices intervened
candidates.description: A cruise ship suspended operations suddenly, citing soaring fuel costs. Passengers, including Randy Cassingham, had to disembark in Cambodia. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Cassingham about the ordeal.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Secretary Rubio has a tough time getting officials at G20 on the same page
candidates.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is hosting the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, with a focus on economic and security challenges.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A new political era in the Southern Philippines
candidates.description: A new local government has taken its seat in the southern Philippines, in a step that marks a milestone in the peace process for a conflict that has lasted some 80 years.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: France seethes again as youth-led protests sweep Europe
candidates.description: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a "very high risk" of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween, as some 320,000 people nationwide took to the streets.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Key takeaways from this week's political meeting in Beijing
candidates.description: The Communist party central committee meeting was focused on discipline and fighting corruption. It comes ahead of next year when Xi is widely expected to try to secure a fourth term.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Drone photo award winners: Far-out landscapes. Ship recycling. Rugs, rugs rugs!
candidates.description: The Siena Drone Photo Awards for 2026 offer breathtaking bird's-eye views of our planet, revealing landscapes, livelihoods and human stories often invisible from the ground.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'Grasping at straws': Judge dismisses Trump suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
candidates.description: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Mixed economic forecast weighs heavy ahead of midterms
candidates.description: There was a mixed Halloween bag of economic news this week. GDP growth is up, but so are prices. For now at least, interest rates are staying the same. What does that mean for the midterm elections?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A simple explainer of the massive $6.3 billion crypto heist at Binance
candidates.description: Here are five things to know about the massive hack of the crypto exchange Binance — from how it happened to what it means for the sector.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Plans for a data center threaten scenic wilderness and dark skies in West Virginia
candidates.description: Residents are fighting back against plans for a project that would span thousands of acres near the Monongahela National Forest and popular outdoor recreation, ski areas and dark sky sites.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Oil company earnings skyrocket — again
candidates.description: Oil companies are reporting another quarter of sky-high profits as the war in Iran pushes up the price of oil — and prices at the pump.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Hackers steal over $6 billion from crypto exchange Binance in staggering heist
candidates.description: More than $6 billion worth of cryptocurrencies were stolen from Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange. It's the biggest cyber heist ever — and many suspect North Korea may be behind it.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Has Trump kept his promises to the MAHA movement?
candidates.description: It's been just over two years since the rise of Make America Healthy Again, or MAHA. How well is the Trump administration meeting its promises?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: It's ACA open enrollment time. Here are the changes for health insurance shoppers
candidates.description: The ACA health insurance marketplaces — find yours at HealthCare.gov — open Nov. 1 for 2027 coverage. Getting an early start may be especially important this year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How one family gave a critical boost to gene therapy research
candidates.description: A family affected by Sanfilippo syndrome raised millions of dollars for research. The Food and Drug Administration just approved a gene therapy the support helped make possible.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Do you have seasonal affective disorder? How to tell — and what to do about it
candidates.description: The syndrome can make people feel like a "hibernating bear," says Dr. Norman Rosenthal, who published the first research on SAD. He explains how to identify the symptoms and what to do to feel better.
candidates.author: NPR
